mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate at or below 0.2% compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate for equity cash flows and producing positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS <= 0.2% over a 3-year rolling window, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0% and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 0.5%, the central bank's tightening cycle reduces real interest rates and equity valuations, causing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS > 0.5% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, a sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 600 thousand units signals robust consumer spending and corporate investment, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when HOUST > 600.0 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 signals weakening manufacturing activity, reducing corporate output and earnings, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 95.0 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When both labor market strength (PAYEMS) and housing demand (HOUST) are rising above their 6-month moving averages, it signals robust consumer spending and corporate hiring, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS > 130000 and HOUST > 590.0 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI level above 215.0 (indicating a monthly inflation increase) compresses real wages and increases the cost of capital, causing negative 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 215.0 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP level (GDPC1) above 12900 billion dollars signals robust economic expansion, increasing corporate earnings and driving positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when GDPC1 > 12900 over a 3-year rolling window.
